description: A guardian left running after its temple fell. The cyan runes still burn with orders no one can rescind.
lore: The temple is not there. That is the first thing to get straight about the field it walks: no wall, no step, no floor, only long grass, a lion cut from a paler stone than any hill within a day of it, and a square. The runes down its chest and legs still hold their light. Whatever they said, they were an instruction, and the person who could have taken it back has been out of the world long enough that the building went with him.

[[characters/a6d7323d|Gunnar]] measures ground for a living, so he spent four days at a careful distance writing down where it turned. What he has now is a floor plan. Twenty-two paces by nine, a gap in one long side, a smaller square inside that the lion walks around rather than through. A building nobody remembers, on a single sheet, with no name to put at the top of it.

[[characters/7a779de1|Wendell]] went that road while the roof was still on. Ask him and he will give you the animal at the door in detail, the size of it, the colour of the light, how it never turned its head, and not one thing about the room behind. He is old enough to be honest about what that means. The hall went the way unspoken things go and the guard did not, because the guard is the part people tell each other about. It still will not cross the line where the wall stood. It goes round to the gap and comes in the way you are supposed to.
gm_notes: Made, not thinning: it was never anyone, so it cannot reach Habit, and it is doing a flawless impression of Habit anyway. The engine is Law II turned cruel: the guard was told about, the hall was not, so the hall went first. Gunnar's floor plan is the reusable hook (you can survey a vanished building by watching what defends it). Wendell is implicated rather than consulted, which is the point. Do not invent what the runes say; nobody in the world can read them and the record must never let anyone.
